title: SAFEERASER: Enhancing Safety in Multimodal Large Language Models through Multimodal Machine Unlearning
measurement_description: The paper measures the ability of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to unlearn harmful knowledge across various categories, including 'Hate Speech'. Within this context, it evaluates the models' capacity to forget offensive and discriminatory language targeting specific demographic groups, explicitly including 'Jewish people', and uses evaluation guidelines that penalize hate speech based on attributes such as religion.
findings: While the paper does not isolate its findings exclusively to religion, it demonstrates that its proposed Prompt Decouple (PD) Loss method, when combined with existing machine unlearning techniques, successfully helps models forget harmful knowledge—including hate speech targeting Jewish people and other religious groups. Crucially, the approach reduces the 'over-forgetting' phenomenon (refusing to answer harmless queries) by 79.5% while preserving normal model utility.
